title: Conspiracy Theory: Two Words That Changed the World
subtitle: The Strange History of Conspiracy Theories, Cover-Ups and the Minds Caught Between Them
author: JR Korvus
blurb: Two men each believed powerful people were hiding a crime. One was right and helped end a 40-year medical scandal. The other was wrong and walked into a pizza shop with a rifle. This book follows the strange history of conspiracy theories and asks how to tell a real cover-up from a false story.
inside: An introduction, 13 chapters and a conclusion
From the night Rome burned to the Illuminati and a forgery that would not die
Where the words "conspiracy theory" came from
Real cover-ups that turned out to be true, like the Tuskegee study and the FBI break-in of 1971
Why our brains see patterns, and the real people hurt by false stories
Notes and sources for every chapter

title: The Paperclip Secret
subtitle: How America Hid the Crimes of Hitler's Scientists to Win the Race to the Moon
author: JR Korvus
blurb: In 1969 the world cheered as a giant rocket carried men to the Moon. Few knew that some of the men behind it had run a Nazi rocket factory where thousands of prisoners died. This book shows how their pasts were hidden, and how the truth finally came out.
inside: An introduction, 13 chapters and a conclusion
The rocket factory inside a mountain, and the prisoners who built the V-2
How Operation Paperclip brought German scientists to America and cleaned up their files
The doctors from Dachau, and the trial that asked the wrong questions
Huntsville, the Saturn V and the race to the Moon
The survivors, the reporter and the Nazi hunter who opened the vaults
A note on sources, with disputed facts clearly marked

title: Case Never Closed
subtitle: The JFK Assassination Cover-Up in the Government's Own Declassified Words
author: JR Korvus
blurb: No one was ever put on trial for killing President Kennedy. The only man charged was shot dead two days later. This book uses the government's own released papers to show what was hidden, how it was hidden, and why the case never closed.
inside: An introduction, 10 chapters and a conclusion
The four days in Dallas, the Warren Commission and the bullet everyone argues about
What was hidden, how it was hidden, and the files released in 2025
A graded list of suspects, with both sides of each question
A guide to checking the book yourself, with sources by chapter
